audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers gave all seven rows to Zaahen while the content whys directly beside them said 'Level 1 is even', 'Level 2 is his', 'Level 3 stays his', 'Level 6 is even' and 'Late settles to skill'.
audit.why: The packet levelChart and the audited mirror agree on Skill / Locke / Locke / Zaahen / Skill / Zaahen / Skill. Locke owns levels 2-3 on his mark-consuming autos and a 10s blink; Zaahen takes 4-5 and first item.
audit.corrected: Rows 0, 1, 2, 4 and 6 flipped as matched full+content pairs, ratings set to the inverse of the mirror's (5, 3.5/10, 3.5/10, 6/10, 5/10, 6/10, 5/10), and the five contradicted phases[N].why rewritten.

audit.whatIsWrong: The single biggest interaction in this matchup is missing: Locke's R grounds. The page describes it only as an execute totem and never says it shuts off your E dash. Separately, Zaahen's W is described four times as 'W Ominous Return drain', a sustain tool. His W is an 850-range pull with no healing at all; his healing is on Q and R. His R is also called a 'lock' that 'traps him' — it has no crowd control.
audit.why: Riot's text for Zaahen W: 'stabs in a direction, damaging enemies hit, then pulls them toward him.' Zaahen R: 'rises then stabs downward, damaging enemies and healing for a portion of the damage dealt.' Locke's R carries the grounding flag alongside execute and slow, which means the disengage the page recommends — leaving the zone — is exactly what you cannot do once it lands.
audit.corrected: Grounding written into phases[4].why, breakdown.cooldowns and 'late'; the fabricated W drain replaced with the real Q/R heals in whys[5], spikes[3].text and 'late'; the R 'lock' claim corrected in spikes[2].text and wants.you[2].

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldowns anywhere for Locke, and 'his E resets on takedowns' is asserted with nothing behind it.
audit.why: Riot's text for Ashen Pursuit says only that he teleports then dashes to attack his next target — no reset clause. The real numbers are Q 10/9/8/7/6 at 950, W 18/17/16/15/14, E a flat 10 at 425, R 120/100/80 at 1000.
audit.corrected: Real cooldowns and ranges written into breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d and the phase whys; the unsupported reset claim dropped.

audit.whatIsWrong: report[8] says 'Anti-heal is optional — his sustain is self-refund, not lifesteal', but the repo flags this matchup as needing anti-heal.
audit.why: Soul Ignition heals back a portion of the damage he takes during the effect. Grievous Wounds reduces healing regardless of its source, so a self-refund is exactly what it cuts.
audit.corrected: Grievous Wounds written into spikes[0].text. report[8] itself is left for a human — see notes.

notes:
Two name problems a human should settle. (1) The page calls Locke's Q 'Ritual Nails'; Riot's own description says he readies 'a set of Soul Nails'. The packet's enemyAbilities is null for Locke, so I could not confirm the ability's display name and referred to it as 'his Q' rather than pick. (2) Zaahen's ability names are unverifiable from his kit file, which carries slots only; 'Darkin Glaive', 'Golden Onslaught', 'Final Retribution' and 'Ominous Return' all appear in this page's content layer with no source. 'Ominous Return' is additionally attached to a drain effect Zaahen's W does not have.

report[8] currently says 'Anti-heal is optional — his sustain is self-refund, not lifesteal'. The repo's own missing-interactions flags this matchup as needs-antiheal, and Grievous Wounds cuts healing regardless of source. I did not edit report[8] because the sentence is a deliberate build call rather than a mechanical error, and reversing a stated itemisation recommendation felt like a human decision.
